_comment: Desired state for branch protection on the default branch. This file is CANONICAL:
the live GitHub configuration is compared against it by tools/checks/branch-protection.sh
(RULE-GOV-001), so a protection silently disabled in the web UI is detectable.
Apply or re-apply with:  tools/apply-ruleset.sh
Scope note (decision F4 in docs/plan/phase-0-2.md): F4 asked for a required status check
AND continued direct pushes to main. CORRECTED 2026-08-14 — those are not both
achievable with this ruleset. required_status_checks DOES reject a direct push to main:
a fresh commit has no check runs, so the push is declined.
The 2026-08-04 test that appeared to show otherwise was invalid: it pushed a NEW branch
matching the rule, which is branch creation rather than a push onto a protected branch.
In practice everything has gone through a pull request anyway, so the working half of
F4 holds and the other half does not. Whether to keep this (PR-only) or drop
required_status_checks and rely solely on deploy.yml gating is an open decision -
see docs/plan/STATUS.md.
Defence in depth, not a single control:
- required_status_checks stops a red pull request being merged;
- deploy.yml runs the same verify job before build-and-push and deploy, so a direct
push that fails verification builds and ships nothing;
- non_fast_forward and deletion protect the branch history itself.
Required-reviewer enforcement is impossible with a single maintainer and is recorded as
RISK-GOV-001 in rules/ledger.yaml, with a re-open trigger.
name: main-protection
